verses.text: Then Eliphaz from Teman answered:
"Would a wise man answer with empty ideas, and fill himself with hot air?
Would he argue with useless words and speeches that do no good?
But you are even destroying respect for God, and stopping people from praying to him.
Your sin is teaching your mouth what to say. You choose to speak like a tricky person.
Your own mouth proves you guilty, not mine. Your own lips speak against you.
Are you the first person ever born? Were you made before the hills?
Do you listen in on God's secret meetings? Do you think you are the only wise one?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not?
Old men with gray hair are on our side, men even older than your father.
Are God's comforts not enough for you, the gentle words spoken to you?
Why has your heart carried you away? Why do your eyes flash with anger,
so that you turn your anger against God and pour out such words from your mouth?
What is a human, that he could be pure? What is anyone born of a woman, that he could be right before God?
Look, God does not trust even his holy angels. Even the heavens are not pure in his sight.
How much less a person who is disgusting and evil, who drinks up sin like water!
Listen to me, and I will explain. I will tell you what I have seen,
what wise men have taught, passed down from their ancestors without hiding anything.
The land was given to their ancestors alone, and no foreigner lived among them.
An evil person suffers pain all his life, all the years set aside for the cruel.
Terrible sounds fill his ears. When things seem peaceful, the destroyer attacks him.
He does not believe he will escape the darkness. A sword is waiting for him.
He wanders around looking for food, asking, 'Where is it?' He knows the day of darkness is near.
Trouble and suffering terrify him. They overpower him like a king ready to attack.
This is because he shook his fist at God and acted proudly against the Almighty.
He stubbornly charged at God with a thick, strong shield.
His face is covered with fat, and his waist is thick with it.
He will live in ruined towns, in houses where no one lives, houses about to fall into piles of rubble.
He will not stay rich. His wealth will not last, and his property will not spread over the land.
He will not escape the darkness. A flame will dry up his shoots, and the breath of God's mouth will carry him away.
Let him not fool himself by trusting in what is worthless, because he will get nothing worthwhile in return.
He will be paid in full before his time, and his branches will not stay green.
He will be like a vine that drops its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
The company of godless people will have no children, and fire will burn up the homes of those who love bribes.
They plan trouble and give birth to evil. Their hearts are always planning lies."
